newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam coffee sales up ahead of Chinese New Year.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee sales up ahead of Chinese New Year.

text.p: Vietnamese coffee sales have picked up steam ahead of the Chinese Lunar New Year festivities in early February, Southeast Asian traders said on Tuesday.
"There's tremendous congestion at the ports in Ho Chi Minh," one trader said, adding the risk of delays will grow in the rush to get shipments out before the holidays on February 7 and 8.
"The problem is that the workers will stop working to celebrate Tet (New Year) by February 5. After that, they'll get drunk," he added.

Of the estimated 240,000 to 250,000 tonnes of coffee to be exported by Vietnam in the 1996/97 (November/January) harvest season, about half was reported to have been already sold or shipped to roasters, traders said.
"By Chinese New Year, I believe two-thirds of the crop would have been exported," one dealer said.
Vietnam's benchmark Grade 2, 8.0 percent black and broken, was seen being traded between US$1,000-$1,100 a tonne FOB Saigon, up from last week's $950, traders said.
"I bought something recently for $1,020 a tonne. I'll be happy to pay today $1,100," one coffee dealer said.

Indonesia's coffee crop appears to be in good shape although most traders said it was too early to make an accurate assessment and they would rather await the results of crop surveys due to be completed by late February or early March.
Indonesia's benchmark Grade 4 coffee was being quoted by regional dealers at around $1,250-$1,300 a tonne FOB Panjang from $1,150 last week.
"You can get small quantities of 50-100 tonnes of Indonesian coffee," a trader said.

Only 40 tonnes were traded on Monday on the Singapore Commodity Exchange's (SICOM) May robusta coffee contract. the settlement price was $1,209 a tonne. No trades were reported on Friday, the exchange said.
